pointsCles: All key metrics (room nights +5%, gross bookings +9%, revenue $7.35B +8%, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.6B +9%) exceeded the high end of guidance despite the Middle East conflict hitting Q2 slightly harder than Q1 (April-May still disrupted, normalization from June confirmed in July); FY26 guidance at constant currency remains in line with the original plan and the long-term algorithm even with 7 of 12 months of conflict impact assumed (gross-bookings top end trimmed only on weaker flight-ticket growth; accommodations unchanged).

AI disintermediation narrative empirically contradicted to date: traffic from LLMs (paid + organic) is still below 1% of room nights and has been stable for quarters - while Booking positions on both sides (OpenAI CPC test group, one of the first partners on Google's agentic booking launched the day of the call, plus proprietary AI journeys: Booking.com AI discovery, Priceline's Penny checkout, Agoda gallery view); internally, customer-service cost per booking falls at a double-digit rate on Voice AI with AI costs kept at low-single-digit % of tech spend under cost-aware model routing.

Record capital returns: $3.7B of buybacks ($4.1B total returned) in the quarter, $7.4B repurchased in H1 at ~$173/share average (post-split), share count down 6% y/y - driving adjusted EPS +15% vs EBITDA +9%; transformation savings target raised a second time to ~$650M run-rate (from $550M, vs $450M at launch), the extra ~$100M mostly from procurement and landing primarily in 2027.

B2B operations of Agoda, Priceline and Booking.com consolidated into a single best-in-class platform led by Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern, targeting large accounts (US banks, airlines, corporate TMCs) with the CFO stressing incrementality discipline to avoid cannibalizing higher-margin B2C; US room nights grew high single digits with direct channel growth, alternative accommodations (+4%, ~37% of Booking.com room nights) remain the stated US priority.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Booking Holdings is the structurally advantaged travel marketplace, and Q2 26 confirmed the creation thesis without amendment: every key metric beat the top of guidance (room nights +5%, gross bookings +9%, revenue +8%, adjusted EBITDA +9%, adjusted EPS 2.54$ +15% vs ~2.45$ consensus), H1 adjusted EPS growth (+14.9%) is running almost exactly on the +15%/yr creation assumption, and the CFO now explicitly targets the TOP of the low-to-mid-teens FY26 EPS guide. The core thesis theme - Booking as AI beneficiary rather than victim - keeps verifying: LLM-originated traffic remains 'significantly under 1%' of room nights and stable, while AI cuts customer-service cost per booking at a double-digit rate. Capital discipline intensifies (7.4bn$ of buybacks in H1 at ~173$/share; share count -3%/yr modeled) and the transformation program was raised a second time to 650M$ run-rate savings (450 at launch). Middle East drag persists on long-haul but normalization began in June.

== THESIS READ ==
- Beat across every guided metric in Q2, and the FY26 EPS guide reaffirmed with the CFO aiming at its top - the model (10.65$) is deliberately aligned there, not above.
- AI story stays an opportunity: sub-1% LLM traffic, direct mix stable mid-60s%, and AI already deflating service costs - the desintermediation bear case keeps not materializing.
- Transformation savings raised again (650M$): the second consecutive upgrade, structurally funding marketing and margin.
- Buyback machine at full throttle (7.4bn$ in H1): the -3%/yr share-count assumption is if anything conservative.
- Watch: gross-bookings top-end trim (flight capacity, Middle East) - immaterial to EPS but the first metric to watch if demand softens.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: ADJUSTED (d-ter) applied consistently - data 2023-2025 carries officially published adjusted net (d-bis correction done at a prior refresh; 2020-2022 remain unverified GAAP, to homogenize only if needed). Bridge (c-ter): the projection chain reconciles EXACTLY at tax 22% + flat -150M$ finNet (net cash building through the horizon); the published 2025 adjusted year leaves a -2,084M$ residual on those projection parameters, flagged in the bridge for a 10-K split (adjusted-basis below-EBIT items). Quarterly EPS (E5 ter) complete with the REAL 2025 seasonal pattern (Q3 ~44% of the year) anchoring the Q3/Q4 26 estimates. Scorecard: FY26 anchor 10.35$ quantified from the initial directional guide (low-to-mid-teens on 9.12$); closed-FY history not sourced at setup; application suspended AND flagged as would-be double-counting (model already at guide top). Deprecated keys purged. WATCH-LIST: (1) Middle East normalization through H2; (2) Q3/Q4 phasing vs the documented 2025 pattern; (3) B2B unit ramp; (4) buyback pace after an exceptional H1; (5) LLM traffic share; (6) ownership/compliance fields still absent from this file (Operation D / next refresh). Next useful refresh: Q3 results (early Nov).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 (early Nov): seasonal peak quarter (validated 2025 pattern), Middle East normalization read, Connected Trip and B2B progression, buyback cadence.

Croissance H1 2026 reelle de l'EPS ajuste (+14,9%, 3,68$ vs 3,20$ estime au S1 25) quasiment identique a l'hypothese de creation (+15%/an) - confirme la trajectoire omniumEPS sans necessiter de revision.

Guidance FY26 gross bookings/CA legerement resserree en haut de fourchette, attribuee a une croissance plus faible des billets d'avion - perspective hebergement inchangee, impact trop marginal pour justifier une revision d'omniumCA.
Impact Moyen-Orient legerement plus marque au T2 qu'au T1 mais normalisation deja engagee en juin, confirmee en juillet - confirme la trajectoire de resolution progressive retenue a la creation.
Objectif d'economies annuelles releve une 2e fois a 650 M$ (vs 550 M$ au T1, 450 M$ au lancement) - soutient la trajectoire de marge/EBIT sur l'horizon de projection.
Rythme de rachats record confirme (7,4 Md$ au S1 2026) - coherent avec la tendance omniumShares -3 a -4%/an retenue a la creation.
Trafic issu des LLM confirme sous 1% des room nights et stable - le risque de desintermediation IA continue de ne PAS se materialiser.
